questions.explain: The CDN build exposes ONE global `Vue` → destructure → `createApp(options)` → inside `setup()` declare refs → **return what the template may use** (only returned names are visible) → `.mount('#app')` always last.

questions.prompt: Which binding set is correct for: conditional class `dark`, reactive image src, two-way text input, Enter-key handler?
questions.explain: Object class binding `{ dark: darkMode }` toggles the class with the boolean. `:` = v-bind shorthand, `@` = v-on shorthand, `v-model` = two-way, `.enter` = key modifier. Mustaches `{{ }}` work only in text content, never in attributes.

questions.prompt: The skills list needs item AND index (the remove button uses the index). Correct v-for?
questions.explain: `v-for="(item, index) in list"`. The empty message renders with `v-if="skillCount === 0"` + `v-else` on the list; `skillCount = computed(() => skills.value.length)` — cached derived value.

questions.prompt: Inside `addSkill()` (script code), how do you push into the `skills` ref and clear the `newSkill` ref?
questions.explain: **Refs are read/written via `.value` in script** (auto-unwrapped only in templates). The array lives at `skills.value`; clear by assigning `newSkill.value = ''`. Also: functions must be RETURNED from setup() to be usable in the template.

questions.prompt: Which statement about `watch` and `reactive` is correct?
options: watch callback signature is (newVal, oldVal); reactive objects mutate via plain property access (no .value)
watch signature is (oldVal, newVal); reactive needs .value
watch only works on computed; reactive is for arrays only
watch fires before the change; reactive objects are immutable
questions.explain: `watch(source, (newVal, oldVal) => …)` — NEW first. `reactive({...})` gives object reactivity without `.value` (`user.age++`); but a **ref holding an object** still goes through `.value` first (`user2.value.age`).

questions.source: MCQ Bank Q22 — v-if vs v-show
questions.prompt: v-if vs v-show — which is TRUE?
options: v-if adds/removes the element from the DOM; v-show keeps it rendered and toggles CSS display
v-show removes the element from the DOM
questions.explain: **v-if** = DOM add/remove (use for rare toggles); **v-show** = `display:none` toggle (cheap for frequent toggles).

questions.source: MCQ Bank Q23 — computed vs method
questions.prompt: A computed property differs from a method because a computed property:
options: Is cached and re-evaluates only when its dependencies change
questions.explain: **Computed = cached, dependency-tracked**; a method re-runs on every call. Use computed for derived state like counts and filters.
